---
title: "Where does the ballast go, and how much?"
---


The neutral point from a straight-line fit of `Cm` against `CL` over α = 0–8°
at 6 m/s, then the ballast mass that puts the CG a given static margin ahead of
it. The fit band is used rather than `run_with_stability_derivatives()` because
the lift curve is nonlinear at this Reynolds number and point-wise finite
differences on it scatter the neutral point over hundreds of millimetres; the
band brackets the best-L/D angle. Static margin is not something the plan
specifies, so three values are carried rather than one.

::: {#805a8470 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
V = 6.0
alpha = np.linspace(-15, 15, 121)
p = polars(alpha, V=V)

band = (alpha >= 0) & (alpha <= 8)
dCm_dCL = np.polyfit(np.array(p["CL"])[band], np.array(p["Cm"])[band], 1)[0]
x_np = x_qc_w - dCm_dCL * c_w

mp0 = mass_properties()
print(f"V = {V:.1f} m/s,  Re_c = {p['Re_c']:.0f}")
print(f"dCm/dCL over alpha 0-8 deg = {dCm_dCL:+.4f}")
print(f"neutral point       = {x_np*1e3:6.1f} mm aft of the nose")
print(f"unballasted CG      = {mp0.x_cg*1e3:6.1f} mm aft of the nose"
      f"  ({mp0.mass*1e3:.2f} g)")
print(f"static margin as built, no ballast = "
      f"{(x_np - mp0.x_cg)/c_w*100:+.0f} % MAC")
```

::: {#795147aa .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# Ballast is a point mass; the CG of structure plus ballast is a weighted mean,
# so the mass needed at a station follows from the lever ratio.
def ballast_for(x_cg_target, x_ballast):
    return mp0.mass * (mp0.x_cg - x_cg_target) / (x_cg_target - x_ballast)

x_b = np.linspace(0, x_le_w, 200)
margins = [0.05, 0.10, 0.15]
m_b = {SM: ballast_for(x_np - SM * c_w, x_b) for SM in margins}

for SM in margins:
    x_cg = x_np - SM * c_w
    print(f"SM {SM:4.0%}  (CG {x_cg*1e3:5.1f} mm):  "
          f"{ballast_for(x_cg, 0.0)*1e3:5.2f} g at the nose,  "
          f"{ballast_for(x_cg, x_le_w)*1e3:5.2f} g at the wing leading edge")

m10 = ballast_for(x_np - 0.10 * c_w, 0.0)
print(f"\nat 10% MAC with the ballast on the nose: all-up "
      f"{(mp0.mass + m10)*1e3:.2f} g, wing loading "
      f"{(mp0.mass + m10)*9.81/S_w:.2f} N/m^2")

# What the plan's own ballast would do here, at its best possible station.
dime = mass_properties(m_ballast=2.268e-3, x_ballast=0.0)
print(f"a dime on the nose: {dime.mass*1e3:.2f} g all-up, CG "
      f"{dime.x_cg*1e3:.1f} mm, static margin {(x_np - dime.x_cg)/c_w*100:+.0f} % MAC")
```

**Answer.** On the nose, and about 3 g of it. Unballasted the airframe is
unstable — 12.52 g of foam puts the CG 184.5 mm aft of the nose against a
neutral point at 156.6 mm, a static margin of −32% MAC — because a stabilizer
35% the area of the wing, plus the fin, sit at the end of a 43.8 cm fuselage.
Station matters more than the mass does: 10% MAC costs 3.10 g at the nose but
8.43 g at the wing leading edge, where the plan says to tape the dime. A dime
alone is not enough at this size; 2.27 g on the nose lands the CG at 156.2 mm,
0.4 mm ahead of the neutral point, which is under half a percent of MAC and
stable in name only.
